task.description: Run the full suite per WF-02 Step 4 and write a structured YAML report to test/reports/. Do NOT rest on a single --seed 0 run: ISS-0011 was characterised during REQ-023's run at ~7.5% (3 failures in 40 runs) and DOES reproduce under --seed 0, which three different agents confirmed on three different run sets, so seed pinning is not a deterministic baseline. Run several times across pinned and unpinned seeds and report the actual distribution. Attribute any lone failure at test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121 to ISS-0011 (GitHub #65) explicitly; treat any OTHER failure as a genuine signal requiring diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: the full suite is run multiple times across both pinned and unpinned seeds, with the real distribution reported
actual pass/fail counts and exit codes are quoted verbatim
any failure is attributed to a named root cause with evidence, never 'probably flaky' without reading the output
a structured YAML report is written to test/reports/ following the established naming convention
pre-existing failures unrelated to REQ-027's acceptance criteria are forwarded, not fixed, and do not block this step's PASS

result.summary:
PASS. Full suite run 12 times on feature/WF02-REQ027-20260816 @ 29abd0c8b4c638a6666a606f0117c14d18884d0a, split evenly 6 pinned (`MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test --seed 0`) / 6 unpinned (`MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 mix test`), with the two modes INTERLEAVED rather than run as contiguous blocks. Every command ran under MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2; the resolved target was confirmed verbatim as "DB=letflow_test2 PORT=5462" before any test command, and letflow_test / letflow_dev were never touched. No `docker compose up` was issued -- letflow-postgres-1 was already Up 29 hours (healthy) on 0.0.0.0:5462->5432/tcp.

=== PER-RUN DISTRIBUTION (12 runs: 10 clean, 2 failed, 1 distinct failure mode) ===
  pinned --seed 0 : 6 runs, 5 clean, 1 failed -> 1/6 = 16.7%
  unpinned random : 6 runs, 5 clean, 1 failed -> 1/6 = 16.7%
  overall         : 2/12 = 16.7%
  failing seeds   : 0 (run 04), 446139 (run 10)

run | mode     | seed   | exit | Result line verbatim
 01 | pinned   | 0      | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)
 02 | pinned   | 0      | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)
 03 | unpinned | 206393 | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)
 04 | pinned   | 0      | 2    | Result: 306/307 passed (4/4 properties, 302/303 tests) + "Failed: 1 test"
 05 | unpinned | 46166  | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)
 06 | pinned   | 0      | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)

 11 | pinned   | 0      | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)
 12 | unpinned | 753555 | 0    | Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)

The 10 clean runs match the expected post-REQ-027 reference exactly: "Result: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests)".

=== FAILURE ATTRIBUTION -- ISS-0011 / GitHub #65, NOT caused by REQ-027 ===
All 12 logs were grepped together for ExUnit's failure-header pattern and the unique results sorted: EXACTLY ONE distinct failing test exists across the whole corpus. Per-log header counts confirm 10 logs with 0 headers and runs 04 and 10 with exactly 1 each. Verbatim, identical in both failing runs:

  1) test method short-circuit -- no DB query at all for a non-write method a GET request issues no Ecto query at all (method short-circuit, no DB round-trip) (Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest)
     test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121
     expected no Ecto query for a GET request
     code: refute_received :query_fired, "expected no Ecto query for a GET request"
     stacktrace:
       test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:136: (test)

Attributed to ISS-0011 / GitHub issue #65 (open, pre-existing, introduced by REQ-021), on read evidence not on resemblance:
 (a) Signature matches ISS-0011 character-for-character in both runs -- same module, same file:line 121, same `refute_received :query_fired`, same stacktrace line 136, same "Failed: 1 test" trailer.
 (b) Run 04's log captures the race in the act. The debug lines IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the failure block are foreign queries from other modules' tests (SELECT FROM "approvals"; INSERT INTO "tenants" for slug "bpm-default-tenant-40"; INSERT INTO "users" for "someone-6599"), and IMMEDIATELY AFTER it are more foreign queries (SELECT FROM "groups"; SELECT count(*) FROM "users"; INSERT INTO "tenant_role"; INSERT INTO "tenants"). Other async tests were issuing Repo queries inside the exact window between this test's global :telemetry.attach and its refute_received.
 (c) NOT caused by REQ-027, re-verified structurally in this step rather than trusted from Step 3b: REQ-027's only new `async: true` module, test/letflow/definitions/schemas_test.exs (line 28), greps clean for telemetry|attach|Repo\.|DataCase -- all three hits are prose (lines 12 and 14 are moduledoc, line 205 is a code comment; that test's body is `assert InstanceDefinitionSnapshot.__schema__(:associations) == []`, pure reflection). Zero Repo calls, zero telemetry attaches. REQ-027's other new module, test/letflow/definitions/migrations_test.exs, is `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false` (line 37), so its DB work cannot run concurrently with the flaky test at all.
Forwarded, NOT fixed, per WF-02 Step 4's rule for pre-existing unrelated failures. No test, application, migration or design file was modified by this step. ISS-0011 was not re-filed (it already exists as GitHub #65).

ZERO other failures across 12 runs. No new failure, no regression, nothing dismissed as "probably flaky".

=== STATIC GATES ===
`MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> EXIT CODE 0, zero output.
`MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix format --check-formatted` -> EXIT CODE 0, zero output.

=== COUNT RECONCILIATION ===
Baseline before REQ-027: 271 passed. Observed after: 307 passed (4 properties, 303 tests), delta 36. Per-file counts obtained by actually running each new file alone: schemas_test.exs -> "Result: 22 passed"; migrations_test.exs -> "Result: 14 passed". 271 + 22 + 14 = 307, matching the suite's own Result line exactly.

=== ISS-0015 (port 4000 :eaddrinuse) ===
Did not occur. All 12 logs grepped for "eaddrinuse": count 0 in every one. No environmental abort; all 12 runs produced a real ExUnit Result line.

=== ENVIRONMENT NOTE ===
Suite wall-clock rose from ~4.7s at REQ-023 to 21-41s here. Cause identified, not guessed: migrations_test.exs run alone reports "Finished in 10.8 seconds (0.00s async, 10.8s sync)" for 14 tests because each does real CREATE/DROP SCHEMA work against Postgres. Expected cost of the tenant-schema replay coverage. Also incidentally corroborating: after all runs, letflow_test2's public schema still holds exactly 8 tables (max schema_migrations version 20260816193002) -- neither process_definitions nor instance_definition_snapshots leaked into public, which is the tenant-scoping :prefix guard working.

issues.title: New data for ISS-0011: third independent seed-0 reproduction, and the pinned-vs-unpinned split did NOT reproduce
issues.detail:
Not a new defect -- three observations about ISS-0011 that this step recorded but deliberately did NOT write into docs/issues/ISS-0011.yaml, because this handoff scoped TEST-RUNNER to running and reporting and to committing only its report plus this handoff. Suggested for ORCH to append.

(1) THIRD independent seed-0 reproduction. Run 04 failed under `mix test --seed 0`, exit code 2. ISS-0011's seed-0 claim is now confirmed by three agents across three run sets: TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at REQ-023 Step 3b, TEST-RUNNER at REQ-023 Step 4 run 30, and TEST-RUNNER at REQ-027 Step 4 run 04.

(2) THE PINNED-VS-UNPINNED SPLIT DID NOT REPRODUCE. REQ-023's 40-run sample recorded 3.8% pinned vs 14.3% unpinned and called that direction 'directionally consistent' with the root cause. This session observed 1/6 pinned and 1/6 unpinned -- identical, no split. Stated as an observation, not a claim: with 2 events here and 3 there, neither sample can establish a real difference, and this is evidence the earlier split was sampling noise rather than a property of the defect. Practical guidance is unchanged and reinforced: pinning the seed buys nothing.

(3) Observed rate here was 2/12 = 16.7% versus REQ-023's better-supported 3/40 = 7.5%. Explicitly NOT proposed as a new headline rate -- 2 events in 12 runs is precisely the small-sample trap ISS-0011's own UPDATE block warns about. One mechanism that could genuinely raise it, noted without assertion: REQ-027 adds 22 async tests and the async phase grew from 0.7s to 0.8-1.1s, so modestly more concurrent async work is in flight per run. That would be further exposure of the existing defect, not a new one. This step did not run enough trials to test that and does not claim it.
